newsitem.title: USA: Britain's Howe says democracy has ruined Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Howe says democracy has ruined Ukraine.

text.p: Democracy has done more harm to the Ukraine than Marxism ever did under the former Soviet Union, former British Foreign Secretary Geoffrey Howe said on Tuesday.

Speaking on the emerging markets at an international business seminar here, Lord Howe said investment in the Ukraine carries a political risk that might not be worth the trouble for foreign investors.
"Democracy has done more harm to Ukraine than Marx ever did. And that's sad," he told an audience of lawyers and business executives.
"It is a good example of a country that has so far failed to address significantly a group of problems which are almost unmanageable."

Howe, who was Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's foreign minister in the 1980s, singled out Ukraine as an example of countries destined to endure political and economic chaos during the transition to democracy.
As a result of political instability, he said, foreign investors have watched economic transactions get run aground by indefinite delays or ambushed by corrupt bureaucrats.
The republic was under pressure from the International Monetary Fund to adopt a budget and an accompanying package of tax law reforms in exchange for a $2.5 to $ 3 billion long-term credit.
Passage of the 1997 budget has been delayed for five months because of political squabbling for which the government and the parliament blame each other.
Howe criticized Ukrainian officials for taking the constitutional separation of power too seriously and paralyzing their country's political system as a result.

"For Ukraine to emerge from the former Soviet Union into a modern economy is to require it to go through the equivalent of what the United States did in 1776, in 1861 and in 1931, almost simultaneously," Howe added.
"There are some political risks that are hardly worth taking on at all."
